sources.entry: PeaZip - Free file archiver utility and open source file compression and encryption tool supporting 200+ formats.

summary.one_liner: PeaZip is a free, open source archive manager and file manager for BSD, Linux, macOS, and Windows that handles 200+ archive formats and offers encryption, hashing, and file-splitting tools.
summary.what_it_does: PeaZip opens, creates, and converts a wide range of archive types, including 7z, rar, zip, tar, gz, bz2, iso, zstandard, and spanned multi-part archives. It can split and join files, edit archive comments, search inside archives, and add files to separate archives. It supports several archive encryption standards, offers file hashing tools, and can export GUI tasks as CLI scripts. The package also includes a file manager with bookmarks, search, an instant content filter, duplicate file detection, and built-in text, hex, and image viewers. A portable version that does not require installation is available.
use_cases: compress files into zip or 7z archives
extract rar, iso, or tar archives
split large files and join parts
automate archive tasks with CLI scripts
how_to_run: Download a release package from the project's Downloads page or Releases section
Install the package for your platform, or use the portable package without installation
Source snapshots are available as peazip-x.y.z.src.zip in the Releases section
Build from sources using the instructions on the Sources webpage
notable: Supports 200+ archive types and variants, including spanned archives (001, r01, z01)
Runs natively on BSD, Linux (x86-64 and aarch64), macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon), and Windows (x86 and x86-64)
Portable package that does not require installation
Can export GUI tasks as CLI scripts
Includes an integrated file manager with duplicate detection and built-in viewers
caveats: Windows builds are also said to be compatible with Wine and ReactOS, which are not the primary targets
Building from source requires following the separate instructions on the Sources webpage, which the README does not detail
